Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor—encapsulated within a GalNAc–lipid nanoparticle—leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. candidates.title: Coherence enhancement through equilibration to near-zero optical temperatures
candidates.authors: Abraham M. Berman Bradley, Mahmoud A. Selim, Hediyeh M. Dinani, Do-Hyeok Jeon, Yunxuan Wei, Huizhong Ren, Georgios G. Pyrialakos, Ulf Peschel, Demetrios N. Christodoulides, Mercedeh Khajavikhan
candidates.abstract: The conservation of phase-space volume in Hamiltonian systems rules out a host of desirable processes across the physical sciences, forbidding the enhancement of radiance through linear and passive optical elements and purification of incoherent states through unitary transformations in isolated settings. Apparent violations are typically sought using gain media and active feedback. Here we introduce an entropic framework that harnesses a fully conservative mechanism, whereby nonlinearity reshapes phase space to relax a multimode system into a pure ground state, even when excited with strongly incoherent inputs. The resulting near-zero-temperature state exhibits minimal statistical fluctuations without the need for active phase alignment. We experimentally observe this behaviour in nonlinear photonic mesh lattices, where efficient spatial coherence enhancement manifests despite the irreversible maximization of entropy. The generality of the underlying mechanism amongst conservative weakly nonlinear multimode systems suggests broad applicability across disciplines, from high-brightness laser sources to controlled condensation in many-body quantum systems such as Bose–Einstein condensates. Phase-space conservation bars coherence enhancement in passive linear optics, a limit often bypassed by gain or feedback. Here conservative nonlinearity reshapes phase space, thermodynamically driving incoherent light towards a coherent equilibrium.

candidates.title: Spatiotemporal intensity-cycling microscopy unveils many-body interactions and correlated transport in van der Waals semiconductors
candidates.authors: Jakhangirkhodja A. Tulyagankhodjaev, Michelle E. Reynoso, Yongseok Hong, Haowen Su, Yoonseo Nah, Shan-Wen Cheng, André L. Koch Liston, Xavier Roy, Milan Delor
candidates.abstract: Spatiotemporal optical microscopies are powerful tools to image the propagation of energy carriers in materials, including electrons, excitons, magnons and polaritons, providing key functional metrics inaccessible to contact-based transport measurements. Nevertheless, these approaches do not distinguish single-particle from multi-particle quantum states, hindering the study of many-body correlations that underlie the complex phase diagrams at the heart of contemporary materials research. Here we extend a concept derived from multidimensional spectroscopy, called intensity cycling, to the spatiotemporal domain using transient scattering microscopy. We leverage this approach to selectively image single-particle and multi-particle transport in van der Waals semiconductors. We demonstrate a series of sought-after capabilities, including clean isolation of single-particle charge transport with high signal-to-noise ratio, spatiotemporal tracking of exciton–exciton annihilation, high-throughput mapping of dielectric disorder, and imaging the emergence of a polaronic Mott transition and correlated transport in a superatomic solid. This work delivers a precision tool capable of visualizing how many-body interactions shape material function. Intensity-cycling spatiotemporal microscopy separates single-particle and multi-particle transport, enabling imaging of charge mobility, exciton interactions, and correlated many-body states in van der Waals semiconductors, including Mott transitions.

candidates.title: In situ CAR engineering and nanoparticle-mediated TREM2 degradation for macrophage reprogramming in malignant ascites
candidates.authors: Yijia Li, Ting Yang, Xiyue Zhang, Rui Peng, Jifang Gong, Zihan Zhang, Bin Ma, Yu Hou, Yunxuan Liu, Kemeng Chen, Qidong Bai, Yian Fang, Changdi Cao, Jia Hao, Zhiwei Sun, Ziqiong Jiang, Mengying Dong, Chenlong Wei, Zhongtang Li, Qiang Zhang, Lin Shen, Xueqing Wang, Mi Deng, Changsong Qi, Lei Miao
candidates.abstract: Peritoneal metastasis (PM) and the resulting malignant tumour ascites characterize advanced gastrointestinal cancers, often leading to poor prognosis and limited response to current therapies. Single-cell analysis of patient-derived PM and malignant tumour ascites reveals an approximately 90% enrichment of TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages, which drive CD8+ T cell dysfunction and tumour growth. Here we develop lipid nanoparticles encapsulating mRNA to reprogram these tumour-associated macrophages into chimeric antigen receptor macrophages targeting Claudin18.2-positive tumour ascites. The lipid nanoparticles incorporate a TREM2+ ligand to enhance the targeting of TREM2 macrophages. The piperazine-containing phosphoramide ionizable lipid synergizes with the TREM2 ligand to inhibit ligand dissociation, promoting TREM2 internalization and degradation via lysosomal and autophagosomal pathways. This inhibits AKT signalling and reprograms tumour-associated macrophages towards an antitumour phenotype, enhancing progenitor exhausted and effector memory CD8+ T cell responses, altering the PM transcriptome, and reducing immunosuppression in both malignant tumour ascites and tumours. Combined with PD-1 blockade, this therapy suppresses tumour growth and extends survival in mice, and with matching immunological effects in clinical samples, demonstrates its translational potential for PM immunotherapy. Targeted lipid nanoparticles reprogram TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages in ascitic fluid into chimeric antigen receptor macrophage cells, providing an in situ cell engineering strategy that alters the tumour microenvironment and promotes tumour cell elimination in rodent models.

candidates.abstract: Abstract The role of phonons in cuprates remains controversial, with their complex lattice structure complicating the investigation. Here, we identify phonon modes originating from charge reservoir and superconducting layers of Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ using sub-unit-cell resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy in a scanning transmission electron microscope. We reveal several phonon modes exhibiting layer-specific localization: ~78 meV in-plane modes localized in the CuO 2 planes, ~42 meV hybrid (in-plane and out-of-plane) modes in the CuO 2 planes, and ~38 meV hybrid modes in the BiO layers. We also observe a periodic modulation of phonon frequencies induced by the superstructure, spatially correlating with the superconducting gap variation. Our findings offer new insights into the lattice dynamics in cuprates, fostering deeper exploration of the microscopic linkage between structural modulation, electronic inhomogeneity, and electron-phonon coupling.

candidates.title: Full-sunlight-driven photocatalytic recovery of critical metals from spent lithium-ion batteries via organic acid leaching
candidates.authors: Sunghyun Ko, Jinha Jang, Janghoon Kang, Wonyong Choi, Ung Lee, Da Hye Won, Jiheong Kang, Giyeong Son, Chang Hyun Kim, Chan Beum Park, Changsoo Kim
candidates.abstract: The rapidly increasing deployment of secondary batteries has intensified pressures on resource security and waste management, exposing fundamental limitations of current battery recycling technologies that require intensive use of energy and chemicals. To enable sustainable battery waste management, systems must improve economic and environmental feasibility at the process level while retaining versatility toward diverse cathode chemistries. Here, we report a sunlight-driven photocatalytic leaching framework that enables robust recovery of critical metals from diverse commercial cathode materials. The process couples mild organic acids with a reusable photocatalyst to orchestrate a twofold leaching mechanism driven by sunlight, in which hydrogen peroxide is generated in situ across the solar spectrum and further activated by UV components to enhance metal extraction without external oxidizing agents. Importantly, the system maintains consistent performance over multiple operation cycles, supporting process robustness and scalability. Beyond its technical performance, techno-economic and life cycle analyses demonstrate clear advantages over conventional recycling methods, including lower energy inputs and reduced greenhouse gas emissions. This work establishes a versatile, profitable, and environmentally benign approach to battery recycling, offering a scalable pathway toward a sustainable circular economy. Researchers developed a light-driven method using organic acids to recover critical metals from used lithium-ion batteries, offering a more sustainable route for battery recycling powered by natural sunlight.

candidates.abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. (Funded by Shenyang Science Tech Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657470) Medium-vessel occlusion accounts for a substantial proportion of acute ischemic stroke cases, yet optimal reperfusion treatment strategies remain unclear for patients ineligible for mechanical endovascular thrombectomy. Here, the authors show that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increases reperfusion rates for medium-vessel occlusion with acceptable safety, although statistically-significant improvements in 90-day functional outcomes were not detected in this phase-2 randomized trial.

candidates.title: Estimating the resilience of non-stationary systems
candidates.authors: Taylor Smith, Andreas Morr, Christof Schötz, Niklas Boers
candidates.abstract: Abstract A wide body of work has applied the concept of critical slowing down to estimate the stability of different Earth system components. Most of them – such as global vegetation – are inherently non-stationary, for example due to strong seasonal forcing that complicates the estimation of their resilience to external perturbations. Here, we introduce a method to account for non-stationarity in estimating the resilience of diverse synthetic and real-world systems via a regression-based formulation of the Langevin equation. Our method does not require extensive data pre-processing, is robust to gaps in the data record, and does not require regular time sampling. We further show that our method can incorporate time-varying data uncertainties, derive uncertainty bounds for stability estimates, and can be natively extended to examine spatial systems. Our method is a drop-in replacement for widely-used autocorrelation-based resilience estimates, and can be applied across diverse Earth system components.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) offer exceptional colour purity and efficiency for next-generation display applications. Despite the recent advances in device stability, achieving long-term stable PeLEDs under display-relevant conditions remains a critical challenge. The actual device half-life (T 50 ) experimentally measured for visible PeLEDs were in most cases limited to below 1000 h for any given brightness, in contrast to the much longer extrapolated lifetimes reported. Here, we demonstrate stable green PeLEDs with a T 50 lifetime of 1350 h at an initial luminance of 1000 cd m −2 (nits), a maximum energy-conversion efficiency of 28.0%, and a peak external quantum efficiency of 24.5%. The exceptional performance is enabled by the insertion of a fluorinated self-assembled monolayer between the metal oxide and polymeric hole-transport layers. This molecular interlayer leads to Ohmic-like characteristics for charge injection, lowering the operating voltage at ~1000 nits to sub-bandgap levels (~2.1 V) where ion migration is suppressed. The accumulated photon output of our PeLEDs over the course of their T 50 lifespan is found to sharply increase as the driving voltage drops to sub-bandgap values, highlighting the critical role of employing low-voltage device architectures in reaching the 1350-h/1000-nit stability milestone. Finally, a flexible active-matrix PeLED display prototype is developed, showing the potential of the devices for wearable optoelectronics.

candidates.title: Decoherence resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect
candidates.authors: Kunkun Wang, Lei Xiao, Stefano Longhi, Peng Xue
candidates.abstract: Decoherence and dissipation, arising from interactions with the environment, can exert a dual influence on transport in physical systems, suppressing coherent propagation while inducing diffusion and mitigating localization in disordered systems. Non-Hermitian physics offers a distinct scenario, where structured dissipation induces directional bulk-to-boundary transport, known as the non-Hermitian skin effect. Whether such transport can persist, be enhanced, or hindered under decoherence remains a largely open question. Here we experimentally address this question using photonic quantum walks with two tunable prototypical decoherence channels, dephasing and amplitude damping. Under dephasing, the non-Hermitian skin effect survives up to the fully incoherent regime and is observed to even be enhanced by dephasing, yielding drift velocities that exceed those of coherent dynamics. By contrast, amplitude damping shows a pronounced order dependence: applied before the non-Hermitian loss operator, it suppresses and ultimately eliminates the non-Hermitian skin effect in the fully incoherent limit; applied afterward, the non-Hermitian skin effect persists and can be enhanced at sufficiently large loss strengths. Our work bridges quantum and classical non-Hermitian dynamics, demonstrates the resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect to decoherence, and opens avenues for harnessing decoherence to enhance directional transport in noisy, nonequilibrium systems. Decoherence, often viewed as detrimental to coherent transport, can instead enhance the non-Hermitian skin effect, which persists into the fully incoherent regime. Its effect can be tuned by the type and implementation of decoherence.

candidates.authors: Ewan McCulloch, Romain Vasseur, Sarang Gopalakrishnan
candidates.abstract: In charge neutral fluids, such as the Dirac fluid in graphene at the Dirac point, charge transport remains diffusive despite the presence of ballistically propagating sound waves: sound waves ``hydrodynamically decouple'' from the slower charge fluctuations. For quasi-one-dimensional charge neutral fluids, we show that this convective charge diffusion is not smoothly connected to the normal diffusion that arises when momentum conservation is broken by noise (or static impurities). Instead, the charge diffusion constant is a discontinuous function of noise, which (in the weak-noise limit) depends only on the ratio of momentum and energy relaxation rates. We describe the resulting superdiffusion in terms of coupled Burgers equations. We present a general mechanism---hydrodynamic recoupling---by which weak noise can induce singular changes in transport coefficients. Our results highlight the limits of zero-noise extrapolation for predicting dynamical quantities like diffusion constants.

candidates.abstract: Nickelate superconductors provide a valuable new platform for the study of unconventional superconductivity that is complementary to the cuprates. One of the central puzzles about high-temperature superconductors is what factors determine the scale of their superconducting transition temperature ($T_\mathrm{c}$). We observe a weak superfluid stiffness that exhibits an approximately square-root correlation with $T_\mathrm{c}$. We also find a strong interplay between Nd magnetism and the superconducting phase, manifested as a substantial low-temperature suppression of superfluid density. These observations highlight the importance of superconducting phase fluctuations in limiting $T_\mathrm{c}$ and unexpectedly strong coupling between the Nd 4$f$ moments and the superfluid.

candidates.title: Level 2.5 Large Deviations and Uncertainty Relations for Non-Markov Self-Interacting Dynamics
candidates.authors: Francesco Coghi, Amarjit Budhiraja, Juan P. Garrahan
candidates.abstract: We address the general problem of formulating the dynamical large deviations of non-Markovian systems in a closed form. Specifically, we consider a broad class of “self-interacting” jump processes whose dynamics depends on the past through a functional of a state-dependent empirical observable. Exploiting a natural separation of timescales, and under the corresponding mixing conditions, we obtain the exact (so-called “level 2.5”) large deviation joint statistics of the empirical measure over configurations and of the empirical flux of transitions. As an application of this general framework, we derive explicit general bounds on the fluctuations of trajectory observables, generalizing to the non-Markovian case both thermodynamic and kinetic uncertainty relations. We illustrate our theory with simple examples, and discuss potential applications of these results.

candidates.title: Order by Inertia in Spinning Active Matter: Holey Fluids and Spin-Textured Crystals
candidates.authors: Camille Jorge, Denis Bartolo
candidates.abstract: Active matter sustains emergent flows at the expense of preserving structural order. The feedback between structure and viscous flows typically disrupts crystalline and liquid-crystalline organization by amplifying the very deformations they generate. Yet this destabilizing paradigm has recently been challenged by experiments showing that inertial fluid flows can stabilize few-body bound states of active spinners. Whether inertial active matter can sustain genuine cohesion and order at the many-body level, however, remains elusive. Here we investigate two-dimensional assemblies of macroscopic spinners operating at high Reynolds number and uncover two phase transitions leading to the emergence of a dilute percolating fluid and a dense spin-textured crystal. At low density, inertial flows generate two competing interactions: anisotropic attractions and transverse Magnus forces that continuously break and reconfigure bonds. Together they drive a percolation transition toward a dynamically rearranging holey liquid reminiscent of the empty-liquid states observed in equilibrium patchy colloids. At high density, the feedback between spin alignment and particle positions suppresses transverse rearrangements and yields a first-order transition toward a spin-ordered crystal. Our results demonstrate that, beyond the overdamped limit, hydrodynamic feedback can promote rather than destroy collective order, revealing a distinct regime of many-body active matter governed by inertial flows.
